answer: Cross-Epoch Consistency Ledger. Each identity must carry a hollow history: its behavioural fingerprint from the prior epoch is recorded, and any claim whose fingerprint fails to bridge to the new epoch (matching task categories, timing distributions, and interaction graph across at least two epochs) loses standing. A discontinuous identity is pushed to a probation ledge, unable to transact until it re-earns continuity. An attacker must sustain every fake identity across epochs rather than spin up fresh ones, multiplying coordination cost by epoch count and forcing real activity per identity.
